content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The key to a successful digital commerce stack lies in its ability to bypass traditional payment gateways, such as Stripe and PayPal, which often restrict access to countries like Kenya due to regulatory and compliance issues. By leveraging blockchain-based payments and Cloudflare infrastructure, you can create a fully sovereign digital commerce stack that operates independently of these platforms, giving you full control over your online store, payment processing, and data ownership.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack, you will need to choose a suitable blockchain-based payment processor, such as NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and offers a flat fee of 0.5%. You will also need to select a suitable cloud infrastructure provider, such as Cloudflare, which offers a range of services, including hosting, content delivery, and security. Additionally, you will need to choose a suitable database solution, such as Supabase, which offers a range of features, including real-time data synchronization and scalable storage.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you will need to integrate your chosen payment processor with your cloud infrastructure provider. This will involve configuring your payment processor to work with your cloud infrastructure, and setting up a delivery pipeline that can handle payments and deliver digital products to customers. You will also need to configure your database solution to store and manage customer data, as well as product information.

Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you have set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you can go live with your online store. To process your first transaction, you will need to configure your payment processor to work with your cloud infrastructure, and set up a webhook to notify your store of incoming payments. You will also need to configure your database solution to store and manage customer data, as well as product information.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your infrastructure is running, you can scale your online store to meet growing demand. To do this, you will need to configure your cloud infrastructure to handle increased traffic, and optimize your payment and delivery pipeline to reduce latency and improve performance. You will also need to monitor your database solution to ensure that it can handle increased data storage and synchronization.

The most important thing to consider is infrastructure sovereignty, which means having full control over your online store, payment processing, and data ownership. This ensures that you are not reliant on any one platform or service, and can make changes to your infrastructure as needed.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy a sovereign digital commerce stack, follow these steps: choose a suitable blockchain-based payment processor, such as NOWPayments; select a suitable cloud infrastructure provider, such as Cloudflare; choose a suitable database solution, such as Supabase; integrate your payment processor with your cloud infrastructure; configure your payment and delivery pipeline to work with your database solution; go live with your online store; configure your payment processor to work with your cloud infrastructure; set up a webhook to notify your store of incoming payments; configure your database solution to store and manage customer data and product information; monitor your database solution to ensure it can handle increased data storage and synchronization.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the difference between a sovereign digital commerce stack and a traditional e-commerce platform?

A sovereign digital commerce stack is a fully independent online store that operates without relying on any one platform or service, giving you full control over your payment processing, data ownership, and infrastructure. In contrast, traditional e-commerce platforms rely on third-party services to handle payment processing, data storage, and other functions.
How do I choose the right blockchain-based payment processor for my sovereign digital commerce stack?

To choose the right blockchain-based payment processor, consider factors such as supported currencies, fees, and integration requirements. Look for a processor that supports your chosen cryptocurrency and has a flat fee structure to minimize transaction costs.
Can I use a different cloud infrastructure provider besides Cloudflare?

Yes, you can use a different cloud infrastructure provider besides Cloudflare, but make sure it meets your requirements for scalability, security, and performance. Consider factors such as pricing, features, and integrations when selecting a cloud infrastructure provider.
How do I configure my payment and delivery pipeline to work with my chosen database solution?

To configure your payment and delivery pipeline to work with your chosen database solution, you will need to integrate your payment processor with your database solution, and set up a delivery pipeline that can handle payments and deliver digital products to customers. This may involve configuring APIs, setting up webhooks, and optimizing data storage and synchronization.
What is the most important thing to consider when scaling my online store?

The most important thing to consider when scaling your online store is infrastructure performance, which means ensuring that your cloud infrastructure, payment and delivery pipeline, and database solution can handle increased traffic and demand. This may involve optimizing resources, configuring caching, and monitoring for performance bottlenecks.
